intro: You're looking for a visitor visa advisor near you because you want to invite someone to the UK, or you're planning a visit yourself, and you need help getting the application right. Visitor visa advisers help prepare applications showing the purpose of the visit, funds and intention to leave the UK. We can introduce you to a suitable UK immigration adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a visitor visa advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, local guidance on a visitor visa application, whether for family, friends or business.
needs: You want to invite a family member to visit you in the UK and need help showing their visit purpose and ties to their home country.
You're planning a holiday or business trip to the UK and want to make sure your application shows enough funds and a clear intention to leave.
You're unsure whether you need a visitor visa or an ETA, and you want advice on which applies to your nationality.
A previous visitor visa application was refused, and you need help understanding the refusal and preparing a stronger application.
You want to find an adviser near you who is properly regulated to give immigration advice, so you can ask questions face to face.
context_heading: The key thing to understand about visitor visa advice
context: It is a criminal offence to give immigration advice in the UK unless you are qualified and regulated. Advisers must be registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA, formerly the OISC) at the right level for your matter, or be a solicitor, barrister or chartered legal executive authorised by their own regulator. Check the IAA's adviser finder or the SRA register before you share documents or pay.

IAA advisers are registered at levels that limit what they can do, from basic applications to appeals and representation. Ask what level an adviser holds and whether it covers your type of case. For a visitor visa, the adviser should be able to help you present the purpose of the visit, your funds and your ties to your home country clearly.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say who the visa is for and their nationality, so we can introduce you to an adviser who understands the requirements for that country.
Explain the purpose of the visit, such as tourism, family visit or business, and how long the person plans to stay.
Mention whether the visitor has previously applied for a UK visa and whether any application was refused.
Tell us where you are based and whether you would prefer an adviser near you or one who can help remotely.
Note any particular concerns, such as showing funds or proving ties to the home country.
Ask for an introduction to an adviser who is regulated to give immigration advice at the level your case needs.
questions: Are you registered with the Immigration Advice Authority, and at what level?
How will you help me show the purpose of the visit and the visitor's intention to leave the UK?
What documents will we need to prove funds and ties to the home country?
Can you help if the visitor has previously been refused a visa?
What are your fees and how will you charge for your work?
How long do you expect the application to take, and what could cause delays?

faqs.q: Do I need a visitor visa or an ETA to come to the UK?
faqs.a: It depends on your nationality. Some nationalities need a visitor visa, while others can visit with an ETA. An adviser can confirm which applies to you and help with the right application.

faqs.q: Can iComply help me find a visitor visa advisor near me?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you need and we will introduce you to a suitable UK immigration adviser, who will quote you directly. Fees are on application.

faqs.q: How do I check that an adviser is regulated?
faqs.a: You can check the IAA's adviser finder or the SRA register before you share documents or pay. It is a criminal offence to give immigration advice unless the adviser is qualified and regulated.

faqs.q: What should I do if my visitor visa application is refused?
faqs.a: A refusal can often be addressed by understanding the reasons and providing stronger evidence. An adviser can help you look again at the refusal and prepare a new application if appropriate.

extra_heading: Getting ready for a first meeting with a local visitor visa adviser
extra: When you search for a visitor visa advisor near me, the “near me” part usually means you want to sit down with someone rather than deal with everything by email. That is a sensible instinct for a visitor visa, because the strength of an application often lies in small details: how the purpose of the visit is described, how funds are shown, and how the visitor's ties to their home country are evidenced. A face-to-face conversation makes it easier to go through those details together and spot gaps before anything is submitted.

Before that first meeting, gather what you already have: the visitor's passport details, any previous UK visa applications or refusal letters, and a rough picture of how the trip will be funded and where the visitor will stay. You do not need everything in perfect order, but bringing what exists helps the adviser see the full situation quickly. It also helps to write down the questions you most want answered, so the meeting stays focused on what matters to you.

At the meeting, expect the adviser to ask about the visitor's circumstances at home as well as the trip itself, since an application has to show both the purpose of the visit and an intention to leave the UK at the end. Ask them to explain, in plain terms, what evidence they would want and why. If anything about their answers feels vague, or they cannot tell you how they are regulated, that is a good reason to pause and consider someone else.

extra_faqs.q: Can I bring a relative or friend to the first appointment?
extra_faqs.a: Often yes, and it can help if the visitor's circumstances are being described by someone else. Ask the adviser beforehand so they can plan the meeting around it. If the visitor is abroad, a phone or video call may be possible instead.

extra_faqs.q: What if the person visiting does not speak much English?
extra_faqs.a: The application itself is in English, so the adviser will need to work from accurate information. Tell iComply about any language needs when you enquire, so we can introduce you to someone who can handle the conversation comfortably. You may also want to attend the meeting to help explain things.

extra_faqs.q: Is a local adviser necessary, or can this be handled remotely?
extra_faqs.a: A visitor visa application can often be prepared without meeting in person, and many people work with an adviser by phone or video. Searching near me is still useful if you would rather hand over documents and talk things through face to face. Tell us which you prefer and we will introduce you accordingly.
